memory_update.text: AXTI should remain in the Layer 1 universe as the cleanest US-listed InP-substrate candidate, but survival depends on export permits, customer qualification, and evidence that AI optical interconnects are driving revenue.
TSEM is a context/reference name for silicon-photonics foundry capacity; although larger-cap, its reported SiPho revenue growth and capacity investment make it relevant for chokepoint mapping.
MTSI belongs in the underfollowed optical-component lane as a diversified analog/photonic supplier with explicit 1.6T and 3.2T data-center connectivity products.
LWLG is a speculative shadow candidate: include only with explicit verification requirements around foundry PDK integration, customer conversion, revenue, and reliability qualification.

Need a later pass on non-US or non-primary-US-listed pure suppliers such as Aixtron, Sumitomo-related InP exposure, JX Advanced Metals, and Asian epitaxy/laser-wafer suppliers, because US-listed coverage may miss the true bottleneck.

node: Optical interconnect materials: indium phosphide substrates, laser wafers, silicon photonics foundry capacity, and optical-engine inputs
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around upstream optical-interconnect chokepoints. The highest-relevance discovery names are not hyperscalers or switch vendors, but suppliers of InP substrates, silicon-photonics foundry capacity, optical modulator inputs, and high-speed optical IC components. AXTI is the cleanest InP substrate exposure but carries China/export-control and customer-qualification risk. TSEM is a larger but unusually pure silicon-photonics foundry capacity candidate. MTSI is a higher-quality optical component/signal-chain supplier but less obscure. LWLG is a speculative shadow candidate tied to electro-optic polymer modulators and foundry PDK integration, with commercialization evidence still weak.
